headline: In 1999 schools across America banned Pokémon cards.
slides: Pokémon arrived in the US. Within months it was a national craze.
Two versions of the cards were among the top-selling toys of the year.
Rare cards traded for $100 or more. Kids were losing, trading away and fighting over them.
One school's staff spent four hours hunting for a lost $75 card.
Schools in Pennsylvania, New York and beyond banned them.
sources: Sources: Education Week (1999), Maclean's (1999), Mental Floss
